AI_declaration: OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex and Anthropic Claude were used as assistive tools for software development, verification code, manuscript drafting and editing, literature organization, and checks of mathematical derivations. All mathematical arguments, experimental design, numerical results, interpretations and conclusions were independently verified by the author, who takes full responsibility for the work.
data_availability: Code and stored results are supplied in Online Resource 2 for the local snapshot v1.7.2-orf-submission, dated 22 October 2026. The repository is https://github.com/MathiasRodriguezCastro/structure-aware-row-scaling. It retains the independently audited scientific archive v1.3.17-oms-submission and adds a separately identified prospective study: 24 new parameter scenarios from known parents, 360 primary MIP calls, a registered 360-call logging confirmation and 96 rational LP attempts. The scenarios remain within the dispatch family; the confirmation does not add new models or seeds. An additional identified follow-up supplies 630 MIP assignments and one technical repeat on these same scenarios, with new seeds, candidate traces, physical-margin tests, CPLEX/internal-scaling controls and the export-aware selector. It adds no independent scenarios. Its archive is inherited byte-for-byte from the audited research package. The larger fixed-policy confirmation adds 3,840 comparative assignments on 160 generated models, with 3,816 quality-eligible assignments and 24 retained diagnostics. Its raw archive also supplies the separate resource pilot and common-reference acquisition/recovery; their costs are not pooled with the comparative outcomes. The lossless tar/xz archive preserves byte-identical repeated files through ordinary hard links and includes per-file SHA-256 inventories and independent replay programs. The small checked support archive restores cluster installation helpers and the wheel lock; the sealed scientific raw archive remains unchanged. Online Resource 2 includes that exact archived code/data ZIP, its validation record, the new study's inputs, points, logs and independent checks, the current editable documents and a checksum-based inheritance record. Historical internal filenames are retained for traceability. The public experimental baseline v1.2-coap-submission is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23145294, with concept DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20648949. These identifiers describe the earlier baseline, not the later experiments or this submission snapshot. The current snapshot has no separate Zenodo version DOI. Online Resource 1 gives proofs, protocols and reproduction instructions. Saved-result replay requires no commercial optimizer license; it checks the supplied exports, logs, points, rational witnesses, unit conversions and summaries. It also reconstructs the 120 additional named bases. Rebuilding all 1,530 historical bases additionally requires the baseline's fixed-basis-exports.tar.zst (337 MB compressed, 5.18 GB uncompressed). Fresh commercial-solver experiments require the corresponding licenses. Online Resource 2 gives the commands and distinguishes replay from fresh runs.
